text:
ConocoPhillips stock rose 1.85% today, bouncing back from a sharp 4.3% drop two days earlier. The rebound reflects stabilizing oil prices—US crude is holding at $89.53 per barrel—and positive sentiment around dividend stocks after major Wall Street analysts highlighted energy dividends as attractive. The stock is still down 0.7% over the two-week span, suggesting today's move is a partial recovery rather than a breakout.

Geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and Russia-Ukraine conflict are creating underlying support for oil prices. Attacks on Saudi infrastructure by Houthi forces and ongoing disruptions to Russian refining capacity keep energy markets on edge, which props up crude prices and can support companies like ConocoPhillips—even as climate negotiations in the near term add long-term policy uncertainty for the sector.
